headline: Daily research brief — Wednesday, September 30

items.title: TSLA deliveries Friday
items.detail: Q3 deliveries report Friday 10/2 pre-market — the only watchlist binary event inside the two-week window. Tesla's own compiled consensus is 461,974 vehicles; the Street spread is unusually wide at 421,758 to 482,000, and last year's comp (497,099) was tax-credit-inflated. Avoid selling October TSLA premium into it.

items.title: MSFT carries the richest event premium
items.detail: 30-day IV 34.1% against 24.2% realized (+9.9pp on a clean window) — the most event-inflated name on the board, with earnings estimated around 10/27–28. That date is unannounced and unverified; TSLA 10/28 and AAPL 10/29 are confirmed. Avoid selling 30-day premium into all three.

items.title: Diesel squeeze, not crude surplus
items.detail: EIA: distillates drew 2.25M barrels, 14% below the five-year average, while retail diesel hit a record $6.53/gal with an export-ban risk flagged. WTI $90.7 (+1.5%) in steep backwardation after a tanker was struck in Hormuz. The binding constraint is refined product, not crude.

items.title: Quant lab: strongest week in recent runs
items.detail: A Fed tree-SHAR paper on IV forecasting (FEDS 2026.049) scored 83 — integrate; it cuts one-month S&P 500 IV error 13% versus the benchmark. A weekly-VIX HAR framework scored 67 — test as the bar any lab forecaster must clear.

desks.Dividends: MSFT raised to $0.98 (+7.7%, ex-div Nov 19); NVDA's new $0.25 rate pays Oct 1. No watchlist ex-divs in the 4-week window.
desks.Earnings: TSLA deliveries Fri 10/2 pre-market is the only in-window binary event. TSLA 10/28 and AAPL 10/29 confirmed; MSFT ~10/27–28 unannounced.
desks.Futures: EIA: crude +922k bbl, distillates -2.251M bbl (14% below 5-yr avg). WTI $90.7 on geopolitics; retail diesel $6.53/gal, export-ban risk.
desks.Parity: SPX box wave at a record ~$146B, ~70 bps over SOFR; a live SPY box enforces within bid/ask — funding demand, not an arb.
